item.title: How OBJ stopped Gaddafi’s AK-47 convoy at Abuja airport in 2006 – Fani-Kayode
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, Ambassador Olufemi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo refused to let assassinated Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi’s delegation bring high-powered weapons into Abuja in 2006, a decision he said saved lives. Fani-Kayode, a former minister of aviation, gave the account in a Facebook post titled “20 Years Ago With Muammar Ghaddafi!” who had then arrived in Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit. He said he received the Libyan leader at the airport on Obasanjo’s behalf and was detailed to accompany him for four days. “He arrived at the airport with no less than approximately 200 bodyguards, all with sidearms, and at least 100 cars (which had been sent ahead and were parked at the airport) to convey him to Abuja. The boot of each of those cars was filled with AK-47s and all manner of sophisticated weapons,” he said. Fani-Kayode said the convoy was blocked at the gate by Nigerian security personnel and the military. He said Gaddafi, members of his delegation and even his bodyguards would be allowed in with their sidearms, but not the weapons in the boots of the vehicles. After three more failed attempts to leave, he said, the Libyan leader lost his temper. “Ghaddafi totally lost his temper, got out of his car and started walking under the burning sun, past the airport gate and towards Abuja saying that if the cars were not allowed in he would walk there instead. Every single one of his 200 bodyguards and delegation members walked behind him!” he said. He said he called Obasanjo, who was on his way to the airport to travel to Lagos, and told Gaddafi the President was coming to settle the matter himself. Gaddafi agreed to return to the airport. Fani-Kayode said Obasanjo greeted Gaddafi warmly, apologised for the blockage and promised that the gates would be opened. But as he left, the then President whispered an instruction to him. “As he walked past me he bent over and whispered into my ear that under no circumstances would Ghaddafi and his team be allowed in unless they complied with our request that they drop the AK 47’s from the boots of their cars and put them back on their plane,” he said. He said Gaddafi’s Minister of National Security and Head of Protocol had threatened to fly the Libyan leader home and boycott the entire conference if the weapons were not allowed in. The Libyan officials complied after what he described as a “hot encounter and harsh trading of words”. According to him, the weapons were returned to the plane, which Nigerian soldiers then surrounded to ensure they were not smuggled out later. Fani-Kayode said the reason for the President’s firmness became clear at the next cabinet meeting. “As for my boss OBJ, he saved lives on that day by putting his foot down and insisting that the heavy weapons must not be let in because, as I was later told when the matter was discussed at the next cab

item.title: Musk To Give Two SpaceX Shares To ‘Every Child In America’
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns. The world’s richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year. He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work. APRIL 30: Elon Musk arrives to court at the Ronald V. Dellums Federal Building on April 30, 2026 in Oakland, California. (Photo by Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP “I recommend holding on to your shares,” Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could “be worth about a million times the current global economy” if it “succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy.” “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them,” he said. In October, Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be “the first of many.” There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau. The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 on Wednesday, meaning Musk’s gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion. SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion. The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the spacecraft central to Musk’s ambition to colonize Mars. item.title: 2027: ADC’s Babba Kaita Rallies Katsina Voters, Promises LG Autonomy, Anti-Corruption Drive
item.description: The Katsina State Governorship Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) for the 2027 general elections, Senator Ahmad Babba Kaita, has described the forthcoming polls as a crucial battle that Nigerians must pursue with determination and collective strength. Senator Kaita made the declaration while continuing his campaign tour across the Funtua Zone, where he sought the support and confidence of voters ahead of the 2027 elections. Addressing supporters during the campaign engagements, the former federal lawmaker said only Nigerians who are directly affected by governance challenges can fully explain the difficulties facing the country, arguing that the electorate has the power to determine the direction of the nation through their votes. According to him, the growing enthusiasm witnessed during ADC campaigns, including those led by the party’s presidential candidate and former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, demonstrates Nigerians’ desire for a new political direction. Kaita said the reception accorded the ADC across the country, including Katsina State, shows that citizens are prepared to use the ballot box to pursue what he described as positive change. The ADC governorship candidate also disclosed that candidates of the party from the seven North-West states have agreed to implement a common development agenda focused on tackling insecurity, improving education, boosting agriculture, strengthening healthcare delivery, expanding economic opportunities and promoting social development. On his plans for Katsina State, Senator Kaita reiterated his commitment to granting full autonomy to local government areas within his first six months in office if elected. He said his administration would conduct local government elections within the first three months, describing grassroots governance as a critical foundation for effective development. However, Kaita warned that local government administrations and other government institutions under his leadership would be subjected to strict monitoring to prevent abuse and mismanagement of public resources. “We will establish a state-owned Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) that will ensure the judicious management of our resources for the benefit of the people of Katsina State,” he assured. In a statement issued by the Spokesman of Kaita, the ADC campaign train is currently touring the 11 local government areas of Funtua Zone, attracting large crowds of supporters across towns and villages. The statement said residents, including youths, women and community leaders, have continued to welcome the campaign team with prayers, endorsements and assurances of support as the party intensifies its mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections. item.title: New York Postpones Thanksgiving Day Parade Over Major Storm
item.description: New York postponed the iconic Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday over fears of extreme weather, a first in the event’s 100-year history, as a major storm gathers steam on the US East Coast. The brewing “nor’easter” threatens to disrupt plans for millions of people hitting the road and flying around the Thursday holiday, one of the country’s busiest travel seasons. “With severe weather expected on Thanksgiving Day, and out of an abundance of caution, in partnership with the City the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed,” Macy’s told AFP in a statement. A balloon of Buckaroo Bob The Minion rests under protective netting during the inflation of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade balloons on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, on the eve of the parade in New York City, on November 25, 2026. Photo by TIMOTHY A. CLARY / AFP The date change has prompted questions about the thousands of parade participants, including musicians and technical staff, who had made arrangements for a Thursday parade. “Our team is now working through the complex operational logistics required to bring the Parade to life on Saturday,” the company said. The annual parade sees brightly colored balloons travel some 2.5 miles (four kilometers) from Midtown Manhattan to Macy’s Herald Square flagship store on 34th Street. Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. It is the first time in its history that it has been postponed, The New York Post reported. ‘Heartbroken’ New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed press conference on November 25, 2026 in New York City. Manoli Figetakis/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Manoli Figetakis / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) “This will be a heavy storm. We are expecting sustained winds between 30 and 40 miles per hour, with gusts as high as 60 to 65 miles per hour possible,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani told a safety briefing Wednesday. “The National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning as well as a coastal flood warning. “Winds will be strong enough (Thursday) to down tree limbs and power lines.” The worst of the storm will strike later Thursday when strong winds, heavy rain and the evening high tide will overlap, the city warned in a travel advisory. Organizers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade in 1997. Workers prepare a balloon under protective netting during the inflation of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade balloons on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, on the eve of the parade in New York City, on November 25, 2026. Photo by TIMOTHY A. CLARY / AFP Volunteers struggled but failed to keep a tight rein on ropes which constantly threatened to slam into onlookers. item.title: Protesters, FIFA boss, Democrat, spy: People who helped define 2026
item.description: Of the many people who made their mark on 2026, five in particular stand out — from an alleged Chinese spy to FIFA’s troubled president and a Madrid pensioner who became the face of Spain’s housing protests. – Alice Huang – She’s the woman at the heart of the international espionage scandal whose ripple effects are still emerging. Suspected of spying for Beijing, Alice Huang flew under the radar until the explosive revelation of her affair with the chief of US chip giant Nvidia, Jensen Huang. The outcry saw him resign, before being sensationally reinstated just days later after the intervention of US President Donald Trump. Alice Huang — no relation to the leather jacket-clad Jensen — is a former director of Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing company under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese tech firms obtain Nvidia AI chips in violation of US export controls. China denies the spying allegations. Alice Huang has not been seen since the scandal erupted. Details on her life are murky, but the Chinese citizen with a Hong Kong passport was filmed at a Taipei party in 2025 wearing a pink dress as she kissed Jensen Huang on the cheek. His departure on November 12 tanked Nvidia’s market value, sparking infighting within the Trump administration over what officials knew, and raising the spectre of trade clashes with China as the US tightens export controls of advanced AI chips. Nvidia’s shares rose 30 percent after the tech giant announced on November 23 that it had reinstated Huang, with Trump saying he had spoken to the board “directly”, igniting a political backlash and leaving many questions unanswered. – Gianni Infantino – FIFA President Gianni Infantino oversaw a highly successful World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico, even brushing off a controversial episode when USA forward Folarin Balogun had his red card suspended following a direct appeal by Trump. But football is a game of highs and lows, and within weeks Infantino faced calls to stand down over plans to sell stakes in World Cup commercial rights to a company run by the brother of Trump’s son-in-law. The proposal was hastily dropped following opposition led by European confederation UEFA, leaving Infantino’s re-election plans in March 2027 in peril. French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo was UEFA’s late choice as candidate. But he and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima face an uphill task to dislodge Infantino, who has been backed by the Asian, African and South American football federations. – Abdul El-Sayed – Democrat Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim elected to the US Senate following a stunning victory in the race for the Michigan seat during November’s midterm elections. “Michigan, we did it!” El-Sayed said of his win, one of many on a seismic night for his party. item.title: US lists 63 professions eligible for 3-year work visa
item.description: The US has outlined 63 professional categories whose qualified practitioners can apply for a temporary work visa allowing them to take up employment in the country for up to three years. The arrangement, known as the Trade National (TN) visa, is available exclusively to citizens of Canada and Mexico under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). The TN visa allows eligible professionals from the two neighbouring countries to work for US employers in specified occupations, provided they meet the educational, professional and employment requirements attached to their chosen fields. According to the US Department of State, applicants must be citizens of either Canada or Mexico, have a profession recognised under the USMCA list, secure a prearranged job with a US employer and possess the qualifications required for the position. The list covers several professional sectors, including healthcare, engineering, science, education, accounting and other specialised occupations. Some of the professions recognised under the arrangement include accountants, architects, engineers, lawyers, pharmacists, registered nurses, dentists, veterinarians, economists, mathematicians, scientists, university lecturers and computer systems analysts. Other eligible occupations include agriculturalists, biologists, chemists, geologists, meteorologists, psychologists, social workers, urban planners and technical publications writers. However, appearing on the list does not automatically guarantee approval, as applicants must demonstrate that they satisfy the specific educational or professional requirements for their occupations. Most of the listed professions require a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent, although some categories permit alternative qualifications or professional credentials. The US government also requires applicants to provide details of their proposed employment, including their job responsibilities, expected duration of stay, qualifications and remuneration arrangements. Under Section 214.6 of Title 8 of the US Code of Federal Regulations, successful TN applicants can be admitted into the country for a period not exceeding three years. The classification can also be extended, subject to the applicant continuing to meet the relevant requirements. The application process differs slightly between the two eligible nationalities. Canadian citizens can generally apply for TN status at a US port of entry or designated pre-clearance facility without first obtaining a TN visa from a US embassy. Mexican citizens, however, must obtain a TN nonimmigrant visa from a US embassy or consulate before seeking admission into the country. The arrangement was originally introduced under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which came into force in 1994. It was retained when the USMCA replaced NAFTA on July 1, 2020. item.title: ‘We will find a way to win’ insists Pochettino after rocky Man Utd start
item.description: New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino insisted his team would find a way to win games after a tricky start to life at the helm of the Red Devils. United were held to a chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, after a 4-0 thrashing by rivals Liverpool in his first match on Sunday. Man United, 19th in the Premier League, were upset with several refereeing decisions across both matches, but Pochettino said his team had to take responsibility for their situation. “I’m happy to be here,” said Pochettino, when asked about the various decisions that had gone against his team in his first week in charge. “We are here to take responsibility… we are going for sure to improve and to put that team in the place that, because of their history, we deserve to be. “Nothing is easy but we have the energy and I think we have the capacity, and most importantly the players and the power and the energy from our fans that is massive and I think united, all together, I think we will find a way to perform and win games.” United had two goals controversially ruled out against Sporting, but might have won the game were it not for a mistake from goalkeeper Senne Lammens. The Belgian dropped the ball for Colombian striker Luis Suarez to score his second goal of the night, cancelling out Bruno Fernandes’s double against his old side. Lammens also saved a Suarez penalty and then gave away a second penalty, this time scored by the striker. “This type of thing happens, that is football,” said Pochettino. “Football is about making mistakes — I’m going to support always my player if something happens.” The Argentine said Man United’s defenders might have done better to help protect Lammens before he spilled the ball. “When you are a ‘keeper, it’s not easy, that ball. And always you need help from your teammates,” added Pochettino. “But of course, we need to accept, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve in all the small details that for sure we will improve.” The post ‘We will find a way to win’ insists Pochettino after rocky Man Utd start appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Registered Voters Now 100m As INEC Removes 1.6m Invalid Records
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, said it is now managing a verified voter register of over 100 million. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​​⁠⁠‌​‌‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this in Abuja on Wednesday, during the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The update comes as the Commission said it has selected 17,676 polling units for the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) mock accreditation and result upload exercise slated for Saturday, 28 November 2026, ahead of the general election in January 2027. According to him, the Commission removed over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated and deceased records from its supplementary voters’ register – the removal has now brought the total verified National Register of Voters from earlier 103 million to more than 100 million citizens. The INEC chairman said that the invalid 1.6 million records were taken off the list, following the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) and statutory claims and objection audit. He noted that no fewer than 11 million people were registered across the three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) conducted since 2025, while over 10.77 million new registrants were retained. “Beyond hardware and logistics, we must also account for inclusivity and evidentiary clarity. Following three phases of Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) that added over 10.77 million new registrants and an ABIS and statutory claims-and-objections audit that purged over 1.6 million invalid, duplicate, or deceased records, our verified register stands at over 100 million citizens, including 232,658 Persons With Disabilities (PWDs) requiring accessible polling layouts and assistive materials. “This was before we went into claims and objections. When we activated the claim and objection to the display at the registration areas and also through the internet, we received about 311,000 complaints. “We addressed those complaints and we found that about 232,000 of those complaints were found to be genuine and we’ve been able to address those issues,” he said. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan Amupitan added that further inquiry from INEC showed that there were an additional 113 which the commission discovered on its own on the supplementary register. He noted that beyond the new supplementary list, most of the complaints received online bordered on anomalies in the existing national register compiled between 2011 and 2023. item.title: Rewane projects 4.5% growth, urges investors to rethink strategies
item.description: By Onome Onyeme The Chief Executive Officer of Financial Derivatives Company, Bismarck Rewane, has projected Nigeria’s economic growth at between 4.3 and 4.5 per cent in 2027, urging investors to rethink traditional investment strategies and embrace emerging opportunities. Speaking at the 23rd edition of the Alpha Morgan Economic Review, held virtually yesterday, Rewane said changing economic realities, technological innovation and evolving business models were reshaping investment decisions globally. “The rules of the past are no longer the rules of the present, definitely not the rules of the future,” he said, urging investors to embrace innovation, research and emerging industries rather than rely on past market performance. Rewane, who examined global economic developments and Nigeria’s investment outlook, said businesses and investors that failed to adapt to changing realities risked losing relevance. He cited the evolution of global businesses, including Apple, as examples of how innovation and leadership could determine corporate fortunes, stressing that past success was no guarantee of future dominance. Rewane observed increasing participation in the capital market, with more companies raising funds through the market rather than relying solely on commercial bank loans. However, he warned of possible property market bubble risks, particularly amid the rapid expansion of construction and property investments in Lagos. Rewane projected that some companies could record revenue growth of between 25 and 40 per cent, driven by capital investment, expansion and increased operations across Africa. He also projected the Naira to trade between N1,500 and N1,600 per dollar in 2027, while anticipating an end to global interest rate increases. He clarified that the projections represented his personal assessment of economic developments. item.title: Five things to expect in 2027
item.description: Things are set to heat up in 2027. From rising temperatures to Democratic control of the US Congress to another total solar eclipse, here are five events to look out for in the coming year. El Nino in a hotter world With an El Nino cycle among the strongest ever observed, 2027 could break new global temperature records. El Nino is a naturally occurring weather phenomenon that emerges from the Pacific approximately every two to seven years. It shifts global rain patterns and brings higher temperatures to much of the planet, exacerbating rising temperatures caused by climate change. This year’s El Nino has already impacted maize in central America, fishery catches in Peru and sugar and rice production in Southeast Asia. But for harvests in some regions and food price spikes, “the worst is probably yet to come,” according to Kaveh Zahedi, of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization. And these impacts will hit as farmers are already struggling with higher prices linked to the war in Iran, and with international aid reduced around the world. Democrats and Trump The Democratic takeover of both chambers of the US Congress in January promises to transform the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, giving his opponents powerful tools to challenge his agenda — but not a free hand to impose their own. After their sweeping November midterm victory, Democrats plan an early push to ease living costs, including restoring Affordable Care Act insurance subsidies, reversing cuts to health care and rolling back Trump’s tariffs. They also want to end the war in Iran, which has driven up fuel prices. Hakeem Jeffries, poised to become the first black House speaker, will oversee a majority able to put Democratic bills to a vote, shape federal spending and use budget negotiations to press for concessions. Perhaps the more immediate impact will come from congressional investigations. Democratic-led committees can subpoena officials and demand documents on alleged corruption, Trump’s family business dealings, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. Such scrutiny could trigger lengthy court battles. Democrats could also pursue a third impeachment of Trump, although removing him would require a two-thirds Senate majority — a formidable hurdle. In the Senate, Democrats can block Trump’s cabinet and judicial appointments, including any Supreme Court nominee. But most legislation needs 60 Senate votes to overcome procedural obstruction, and Trump can veto measures that reach his desk. Overriding him requires two-thirds majorities in both chambers. The result could be two years of subpoenas, spending standoffs and confrontation, punctuated by possible deals on shared priorities. item.title: Trump, NATO chief urge Russia not to ‘expand’ Ukraine war
item.description: US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued Wednesday after meeting in Florida. The “outstanding” and “very impactful” meeting focused on the wars in Ukraine and Iran, said the statement issued by the White House after the closed-door talks at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. “We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added. The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes despite the US leader describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin. “For us, he is a killer,” Zelensky told CNN. Rutte was asked about Trump’s comments in an interview with Fox News’ “Fox & Friends” on Wednesday. “What President Trump is doing, also in the meeting in Shenzhen, is testing Putin,” the NATO secretary general said. “How serious is he? Is he willing to come to the negotiating table? Is he willing to really engage in talks. “So let’s keep the pressure on. I think it is working, and we have to keep that going.” Trump, accused by critics of siding with Moscow over Kyiv, said following his meeting with Putin that the Russian leader wants to see the war end by “diplomatic means.” The Florida meeting comes as European nations have expressed a desire to join preliminary talks that have so far only included Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Rutte said any agreement is going to have to include security guarantees for Ukraine. “When the war ends, either with a peace deal, preferable, or if not possible, a long-term ceasefire, we need to make sure that Ukraine has the security guarantees going forward,” he said. “But the most important thing here,” Rutte added, “is that we have to make sure that Ukraine has what it needs to keep the fight going, being so successful and putting that maximum pressure on the Russians.” Trump and Rutte also discussed increasing defense spending, which the US president has pressed European powers to do, the joint statement said. The Florida talks also came as Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth is expected to announce in coming weeks a review of the US force presence in Europe. item.title: CBN raises BDC’s dollar cash limit to $1m weekly
item.description: Banks to receive dollar cash from apex bank to meet demand By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has temporarily raised the weekly dollar cash purchase limit for Bureau De Change (BDC) operators from $150,000 to $1 million, as part of measures to address seasonal demand pressures in the foreign exchange market. The apex bank also pledged to supply authorised dealer banks with dollar cash to meet the requirements of their BDC customers, allowing licensed operators to access up to 100 per cent of their foreign exchange purchases in cash. The development was confirmed by bankers and forex dealers who spoke to Vanguard, following an email communication from the CBN on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, outlining the new operational arrangements. Kunle Ezun, Chief Economist, Ecobank Nigeria, confirmed the development, saying: “Very correct. The message was sent yesterday. The banks are putting machinery in place to commence the sale. It will be T+2.” Taiwo Ebenezer, Chairman, Association of Bureaux De Change Operators of Nigeria (ABCON), South-West Zone, also confirmed the directive, saying some banks had already contacted BDC operators. “Yes sir, some banks have been calling. CBN also promised to fund the banks,” he said. In an email dated November 24, 2026, sent by Yasir Shanono Shehu and Aderinola Shonekan, of the CBN, the apex bank said the measures were designed “to address seasonal demand pressures and improve orderly access to US$ cash for end users.” The apex bank stated: “All licensed BDCs (please see attached) may access US$ cash for FX purchased at the NFEM through the Authorised Dealer Banks (ADBs) with which they hold accounts, and the CBN will support ADBs with any cash requirements to meet the demand of their BDC clients.” Under the new arrangement, “the approved licensed BDCs may receive up to 100% of an approved FX purchase in US$ cash from the ADB where they hold their settlement account.” The CBN added that “the weekly purchase cap is temporarily increased from USD 150,000 to a maximum of USD 1 million per BDC.” BDCs are required to submit requests through the BDC FX Purchase Tracker (FXBT), while authorised dealer banks are expected to acknowledge requests same day and confirm or reject them on the portal, stating reasons for any rejection. According to the CBN, “ADBs shall consolidate confirmed cash requirements, which will be validated against the FXBT, after which the CBN will supply US$ cash to the ADBs for onward disbursement to the BDCs.” On settlement, the apex bank said: “Settlement between the CBN, ADBs and BDCs is on a T+2 basis, i.e. two (2) business days after the trade date on which the ADB confirms the request on the FXBT. The BDC’s settlement account shall be debited at the point of cash disbursement.” The CBN, however, said existing documentation and KYC/CDD requirements, the prohibition of third-party transactions and the 24-hour sell-back rule remain in force and apply equally to cash transactions. item.description: By Jimitota Onoyume, Henry Umoru & Egufe Yafugborhi Presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr. Peter Obi, has condemned the killings at Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State during Monday’s rally of the party, describing the incident as tragic and unacceptable. Meanwhile, Omo-Agege has criticised the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue of the rally, alleging that about 50 officers failed to protect members of the party during the attack. Also, the Obidient Movement condemned Monday’s attack, observing that Nigerians can no longer have confidence in a police force that appears more interested in protecting political interests than protecting citizens, stressing that the police derive their authority from the people. Obi said it was disturbing that some people could resort to killing others simply because they want to occupy political positions, assuring the bereaved families that the sacrifices of the victims would not be in vain. “People cannot sacrifice for this in vain. All the sacrifices will not be in vain. We cannot kill or harm people simply because we want to become political leaders,” he said. Obi spoke, Tuesday, night during a condolence visit to the family of the late Moses Anaughe, who was shot dead during the attack. Anaughe, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly representing Ughelli North Constituency I and former Federal Commissioner of the Federal Character Commission, was attacked by the assailants while stepping out of his vehicle. He was allegedly shot at close range. At the deceased’s residence in Agbarho, Obi consoled his widow and was seen sharing playful moments with their young son in an effort to comfort the grieving family. item.title: NLC, TUC feud: How we brokered peace in Ajaero, Osifo’s rift — Obiajulu
item.description: *lSays some individuals exploited situation to tear labour movement apart By Victor Ahiuma-Young The protracted disagreement between the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, over the Federal Government’s N70,000 transport relief agreement with the NLC, which the TUC rejected, threatened to undermine the unity and collective bargaining strength of organised labour. The disagreement escalated into public exchanges and personal attacks between NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and his TUC counterpart, Festus Osifo, raising concerns that the welfare and interests of Nigerian workers were being overshadowed by the leadership crisis. Worried that the feud could further divide the labour movement and weaken its ability to defend workers’ interests, veteran labour leaders, led by pioneer NLC President, Hassan Sunmonu, intervened and brokered peace between the two leaders. Other prominent figures involved in the reconciliation included Dr Peace Obiajulu, Comrades Peter Esele, Ayuba Wabba, Bobboi Kaigama and Quadri Olaleye. In this interview, former TUC President, Dr Obiajulu, recounts what triggered the crisis, how it escalated, and how the intervention of the labour elders helped restore cordial relations between the two labour centres. She reveals that poor communication largely fuelled the disagreement, while some individuals exploited the situation, warning that the crisis nearly tore the labour movement apart and ultimately put workers’ interests at risk. What actually led to the disagreement between the Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress, and how did you get involved in the reconciliation? To start with, I was not even aware that there was a disagreement between the two organisations. I was called by Quadri Olaleye, a former President of TUC. He told me that the President of NLC had asked whether Mrs Obiajulu, whom we fondly call Mummy, had been informed about the meeting. That was when I asked whether there was a problem between TUC and NLC. He said yes. I responded that it was a family matter, just like disagreements between a husband and wife or among children in a family. In all honesty, I do not know who initiated the reconciliation process. I am sure it was the elders. They must have seen what was happening on television and read about it in the newspapers. If I had come across the situation myself, I would equally have reached out to some of the elders to intervene. I would not like to see organised labour become a target of public ridicule. The moment TUC and NLC begin to quarrel or fall apart, workers are left on their own. Whenever there is a problem within the labour movement, workers are the ones who suffer because nobody will be left to speak effectively on their behalf. item.title: Risk of retaining fuel subsidy outweighed political consequences – Idris
item.description: • President misrepresented on electricity supply promise – Onanuga •FG defends power sector reforms, increased revenue to states By Juliet Umeh MINISTER of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the removal of fuel subsidy and unification of exchange rates saved Nigeria from imminent economic collapse. Idris, who spoke at an interactive session with journalists organised by the All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council Media and Strategic Communications team in Lagos, Monday, said the President took politically risky decisions in the overriding interest of the country. He maintained that the reforms had improved government revenues at all levels, strengthened the economy and positioned the country for sustainable growth. He said: “When the President took office in May 2023, there were two major policy decisions. One was doing away with this monster called fuel subsidy. The second was ensuring that the multiple exchange rate regimes that we had in this country were also done away with. “Presidents after presidents, everyone knew that fuel subsidy was a big problem and a big drain on the economy of this country. But no one was able to achieve its removal until President Bola Tinubu came. “It was not a convenient decision for Mr President. In fact, it was politically risky for him, for someone who had just won an election, who had just been sworn in and who had another election staring him in the face.” Idris explained that the administration considered the consequences of retaining the subsidy and concluded that delaying the reforms would have been more damaging to the country. “The risk of waiting any longer far outweighed whatever political risk he, as a person, as a president or as a politician, should take. “This created enough fiscal headroom, not just for the Federal Government but also for the sub-nationals. Federal Government has made a lot more money. Sub-nationals have made a lot more money,” he said. Economy on path to recovery The minister also said international financial institutions and rating agencies had acknowledged improvements in Nigeria’s economic outlook. He said: “The IMF, the World Bank, everybody is saying, yes, we have some challenges as a nation, but our economy is on the path that will lead us to prosperity. “Our GDP is on the rise. Inflation that was becoming a big problem has been curtailed. Headline inflation, food inflation, all are down.” However, journalists at the meeting raised concerns over persistent insecurity, high petrol prices, inadequate electricity supply, distribution of Compressed Natural Gas, CNG, buses and the impact of increased allocations to state governments on citizens’ welfare. item.title: Tinubu vows to sustain peace, defeat insurgency in North-East
item.description: •Promises rescue of abducted Askira Uba schoolchildren •Shettima, Zulum hail security gains, seek second term for Tinubu ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has pledged to sustain the relative peace recorded in Borno State and the North-East, directing security agencies to intensify operations against fleeing insurgents. Tinubu, who spoke yesterday at an All Progressives Congress, APC, rally in Maiduguri ahead of the 2027 general elections, said the security gains achieved by the armed forces would be consolidated and translated into full economic recovery. In a statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, the President commended Borno State Governor, Prof. Babagana Zulum, for restoring hope and transforming the state’s economy. “Let me start by thanking the Governor of the State, Prof. Babagana Zulum. Well done on restoring Borno State and transforming its economy. “You restored our hope by believing that stability will bring development,” he said. Tinubu, who commissioned projects including the National Youth Service Corps Female Lodge and Borno International Conference Centre, said the North-East had witnessed economic improvements in the last three years, with increased investments in education, healthcare and infrastructure. He urged fleeing insurgents to surrender their weapons, assuring troops of continued government support and improved welfare for them and their families. On the abducted schoolchildren from Askira Uba, the President promised intensified intelligence gathering and rescue operations. “I think there’s a point to note here: the abducted children of Askira Uba School. They are there, and with our prayers and intelligence, our armed forces will rescue them, Insha Allah,” he said. Attributing the security gains to cooperation among political leaders, residents, the Federal Government and security agencies, Tinubu thanked the people of Borno for their support and commended Vice-President Kashim Shettima for his loyalty. He also acknowledged former governor Ali Modu Sheriff and other North-East political leaders for their contributions. In his remarks, Shettima urged voters to reject the former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential candidate, questioning his leadership capacity. “You don’t expect someone who could not provide leadership at home by reconciling his own people to provide leadership at a national level,” he said. Shettima urged the electorate to reward Tinubu’s administration with a second term, claiming it had performed well in Borno, Bauchi, Taraba, Adamawa and other states. Earlier, Zulum thanked Tinubu for his interventions in Borno, saying they had contributed to the state’s recovery and economic repositioning. “If someone has done well for you, like our President, then we should give him a good reward. “We have witnessed relative peace in Borno State and the North-East,” he said. item.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
item.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. The country will also push for stronger capacity-building initiatives and the transfer of marine technology to African and other developing nations. Ambassador Ibrahim further noted Nigeria’s support for the establishment and effective operation of a Special Fund with adequate and predictable resources to enable developing countries to implement the agreement.
